status_summary: The executive and rulemaking track is under way, while the Mandate's statutory changes are not. Executive Order 14279 (signed 2025-04-23) directed ED to hold accreditors accountable under the recognition criteria, ensure they do not require discrimination barred by law, ease switching of accreditors, resume recognizing new accreditors and assess the ABA council's recognition; ED published a nonbinding interpretive rule on initial recognition on 2026-02-27 (91 FR 9709). ED published the proposed rule 'Accreditation, Innovation, and Modernization' on 2026-08-20 (91 FR 53940; 34 CFR parts 600, 602 and 668), which among other provisions would state that recognition confers no antitrust immunity (section 602.13), bar standards that force institutions to violate lawful state law (section 602.16), apply First Amendment and viewpoint protections except for religious-mission institutions (sections 602.15 and 602.17) and ease switching of accreditors; comments closed 2026-09-21 with 7,051 received and no final rule has been published. The advisory committee met 2026-09-23 and 2026-09-24 and made no recommendation on the ABA council, and no Higher Education Act amendment or antitrust action was found.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14279 (signed 2025-04-23, published 2025-04-28) directs the Education Secretary to enforce recognition criteria against accreditors, ensure accreditors do not require discrimination barred by law or push violations of state law, streamline switching of accreditors, resume recognizing new accreditors, and assess whether to suspend or end recognition of the ABA's law school accreditation council; it directs the Attorney General to investigate alleged discrimination by ABA-linked law schools.

ED publishes (91 FR 9709) a nonbinding interpretive rule on initial recognition of accreditors, stating its reading of the criteria and review timing for new agencies and citing Executive Order 14279; the rule keeps a two-year period that starts at a new agency's first accrediting activity.

ED publishes the proposed rule (91 FR 53940, 82 pages) 'Accreditation, Innovation, and Modernization' amending 34 CFR parts 600, 602 and 668. It reflects the consensus of the negotiated rulemaking committee (announced 2026-01-27; sessions in April and May 2026; consensus 2026-05-21) and proposes removing geographic limits on accreditors, dropping the two-year rule for initial recognition, barring standards that push institutions to violate federal or state law, requiring viewpoint-neutral decisions except for agencies with a religious mission, and easing institutions' switching of accreditors. Comments closed 2026-09-21 with 7,051 received.

ED publishes (91 FR 54315) a notice of a 2026-09-23 and 2026-09-24 meeting of its accreditation advisory committee (NACIQI) to review renewal of recognition for six agencies, including the ABA's law school accreditation council and the Southern Association's Commission on Colleges, plus one compliance report.

On the second day of its meeting, NACIQI voted 11-1 to report that it could not reach a recommendation on renewing federal recognition of the ABA's law school accreditation council, after two 8-8 votes the previous day; the Under Secretary has 90 days to make a final determination (Higher Ed Dive, 2026-09-25).
